scope: Clinical glossary expansions for atlas metadata; definitions do not interpret individual results or assign diagnoses, resistance categories, prognosis, or treatment.

entries.label: Polymerase chain reaction
entries.definition: Laboratory method that makes many copies of a selected DNA segment so it can be detected or studied.
entries.source_label: NIH NHGRI — Polymerase Chain Reaction Fact Sheet
entries.note: A method label does not establish a positive result, active infection, or availability of a particular assay. RNA testing requires a reverse-transcription step; do not conflate every PCR label with a specific PCR variant.

entries.label: Minimum inhibitory concentration
entries.definition: Laboratory concentration endpoint for inhibition of microbial growth during antimicrobial susceptibility testing.
entries.source_label: EUCAST — Reading guide for broth microdilution, version 5.0 (2024), pages 3 and 19
entries.note: Usually the lowest concentration inhibiting visible growth; specific organism–agent combinations have defined endpoint exceptions. An MIC field alone is not an S/I/R category; interpretation depends on the applicable method and breakpoint.

entries.label: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus
entries.definition: Name for Staphylococcus aureus with methicillin resistance, used in microbiology organism and resistance records.
entries.source_label: CDC — Laboratory Testing for Methicillin (oxacillin)-resistant Staphylococcus aureus
entries.note: Explains the recorded concept only. The presence of this term in atlas metadata does not demonstrate patient carriage, infection, or an individual susceptibility finding.

entries.label: Vancomycin-resistant enterococci
entries.definition: Collective name for enterococci with resistance to vancomycin, used in microbiology organism and resistance records.
entries.note: Enterococci is the plural bacterial-group name. A metadata label alone does not demonstrate patient carriage, infection, or an individual susceptibility finding.

entries.label: Extended-spectrum beta-lactamase
entries.definition: Bacterial enzyme that can break down certain antibiotics; microbiology records may describe organisms that produce these enzymes.
entries.note: ESBL names the enzyme or mechanism; ESBL-producing Enterobacterales names a bacterial group. Do not silently equate an ESBL field with a confirmed patient isolate, active infection, or a complete resistance profile.

entries.label: Cytomegalovirus
entries.definition: Common virus that can remain in the body for life; CMV labels identify related laboratory tests or clinical metadata.
entries.note: A virus or assay label does not establish active infection, reactivation, or CMV disease.

entries.label: Epstein–Barr virus
entries.definition: Herpesvirus also called human herpesvirus 4; it is a cause of infectious mononucleosis and appears in related test labels.
entries.note: A virus or assay label does not establish current infection or an EBV-associated disease.

entries.label: Human immunodeficiency virus
entries.definition: Virus that affects the immune system; HIV labels identify the virus or related laboratory and clinical records.
entries.note: Do not infer HIV infection, test positivity, viral load, or AIDS from the presence of a metadata field.

entries.label: Hepatitis C virus
entries.definition: Virus that causes hepatitis C; the abbreviation can identify virus-related antibody or RNA testing and clinical records.
entries.note: HCV is the virus name, not a test result. Preserve the distinction between antibody and RNA assay labels; metadata does not establish current infection.

entries.label: Hepatitis B surface antigen
entries.definition: Protein on the surface of hepatitis B virus that is measured by a hepatitis B antigen test.
entries.source_label: CDC — Clinical Testing and Diagnosis for Hepatitis B
entries.note: An antigen-test field is not the same as a positive result. Do not infer current infection from field availability or provide patient-level interpretation in this glossary.

entries.label: Antibody to hepatitis B core antigen
entries.definition: Antibody directed against the hepatitis B virus core antigen, measured in hepatitis B serology.
entries.source_label: CDC — Hepatitis B serologic markers, Table 5
entries.note: The unqualified term does not specify total antibody or IgM. Preserve any total, IgM, or IgG qualifier in the source field; do not assign one or infer an infection phase.

entries.label: Intensive care unit
entries.definition: Hospital unit providing close monitoring and specialized care for people with critical illness or injury.
entries.note: A care-location or encounter label does not identify the reason for admission or prove that a specific organ-support treatment occurred.

entries.label: Admission, discharge and transfer
entries.definition: Patient-administration events and messages describing registration, admission, discharge, transfer, and encounter updates.
entries.source_label: HL7 International — Patient Administration (ADT) standard brief
entries.note: HL7 expands ADT as Admit, Discharge, and Transfer. Use this expansion only in the EHR/encounter context; ADT has other clinical meanings outside that context. Operational events are not diagnoses.

entries.label: Chronic lymphocytic leukaemia International Prognostic Index
entries.definition: CLL prognostic score combining age, clinical stage, TP53 status, IGHV mutation status, and serum beta-2 microglobulin.
entries.source_label: International CLL-IPI working group — Original index publication, Lancet Oncology (2016)
entries.note: Describes the score and its components only. The glossary does not calculate a score, assign a risk group, give an individual prognosis, or imply that all components are available in the atlas.

entries.label: Cumulative Illness Rating Scale
entries.definition: Clinical rating scale used to summarize physical illness burden from medical information.
entries.source_label: Conwell et al. — Validation of the Cumulative Illness Rating Scale, Journal of the American Geriatrics Society (1993)
entries.note: Use in the comorbidity-score context. The original instrument title is also verified in Linn et al. (1968), https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/5646906/. CIRS alone does not identify the geriatric adaptation CIRS-G; do not add G, assert a version, or transfer version-specific scoring details without source-field evidence.
